ul.li: Ticket.canTransitionTo() is where diagram 07 lives in code. The state machine is behaviour on the entity, not a lookup table and not a UI concern.

Employee.normalize() is the single source of the FR-13 rule. It must be the same function that computes the stored name_normalized, or the unique index and the lookup will disagree and inline creation (FR-11) starts producing duplicates.

TicketNumberGenerator.scopeKeyFor() is the entire cost of OPEN-1. One method formats a date into either '2026-07-15' or '2026'. Everything downstream — the table, the lock, the uniqueness constraint — is identical under both schemes.

TicketService is the only transaction boundary. It is why AuditLog and SyncOutbox are shown as created by the service rather than by Ticket: they must commit with the change, and an entity cannot guarantee that.

Ticket.isFirstTimeFix() returns status == CLOSED && ongoing_at == null. The department fixes most concerns on the spot, so this — not resolution rate — is the metric that says something interesting about the work.
There is no void() and no reopen(). Closed is terminal; a recurrence is a new ticket. Mis-encoded tickets are corrected via update(), which the audit log records.
Department and MainIssueCategory exist as classes because FR-16 and FR-18 need controlled vocabularies. Their instances come from the IT team — OPEN-4.
